morph.rootq: Cartilla (Aguirre Licht et al. 2013) p.74-76: 'Los lexemas de esta lengua son morfemas autoacentuados así sean monosílabos ... Si dos lexemas forman un compuesto se acentúa el último ... Pero la mayoría de palabras en embera-chamí acentúan la penúltima sílaba, es el patrón silábico. El acento primario de una palabra se va corriendo a la derecha en virtud del arreglo de morfemas inacentuados y autoacentuados: / w'ẽra / hembra → / wẽrárã / hembras → / wẽrar'ãba / por las hembras. Algunos gramemas (palabras gramaticales) son autoacentuados, atraen el acento en la palabra, como el prohibitivo / r'ã / o el alativo, dativo / má / ... pero la mayoría de gramemas son inacentuados / rã / plural de…
morph.elicq: The cartilla gives no statement of how accent was checked; evidence is presented as isolated citation words with phonetic transcriptions (p.77: '/ ãwár / sardina / tatamá / a la abuela / éoroɓá / barro / eterwár / pollito') plus one illustrative sentence for accent groups (p.78: '/ chi ẽbẽrar'ãba imama beatasidáma / los embera mataron al tigre'), and the method statement is only 'Todo el análisis lingüístico fue hecho bajo una perspectiva estructural' (p.~16), with the phonology credited to Aguirre Licht 1995, Fonología del embera-chamí de Cristianía.
morph.stmt: Predominantly suffixing/postposing and agglutinative: Alzate Camacho 2025 p.21 'los guiones dobles señalan la unión del predicado con varios elementos con función gramatical, exhibiendo así el carácter aglutinante del embera', p.22 'la serie de gramemas postverbales', p.26 'Como lengua SOV típica, el embera tiene postposiciones'; the U. Caldas catalogue abstract of Aguirre Licht 1990 (Aspectos gramaticales generales del idioma embera de Cristianía) puts it as 'se puede caracterizar al embera como una lengua ergativa con tendencia a sufijos'. The only prefixal grammemes in the source are bound possessor pronouns (mʉ̃-kima) and the verbal totalizer pe- (pe-ko).

631.sec_quote: Las vocales de las sílabas con el acento primario de las palabras se alargan y se pueden doblar al encuentro con otras sílabas acentuadas. El encuentro de dos sílabas CV acentuadas produce el doblamiento de la vocal de la primera sílaba y el acento primario de la palabra lo porta la segunda sílaba. ... En fonética se marcan los acentos de la palabra, aquí se marcará sólo el acento primario.
631.sec_loc: book p.77 ('El acento') and p.91 ('Convenciones', 'Fonética'); accent chapter pp.74-78 and 'Marcación de acentos' pp.82-84 read in full

secx.sec_quote_tr: The vowels of the syllables bearing the primary accent of words lengthen and may double when they meet other accented syllables. The meeting of two accented CV syllables produces doubling of the vowel of the first syllable, and the primary accent of the word is carried by the second syllable. ... In phonetics the accents of the word are marked; here only the primary accent will be marked.

tn.quote: En general, el tono parece ser mtrs importante que la intensidad (v€ase, por ejemPlo, Rex Y Sch6ttelndreyer L973: 79) en la manifestaci6n fon6tica del acento y ciertas observaciones de Loewen (1958: 20, no:a 4) sugieren incluso la posibilidad de que el samb(r sea una lengua tonal … No obstante, por el momento, todos los autores coinciden en asignar a las lenguas la condici6n de acentuales … En dichas palabras, en los conjuntos de cognados, 6l acento recae en la penfltima silaba casi sin excepciones en saija y chami
tn.translation: In general, pitch seems to be more important than intensity (see, e.g., Rex & Schöttelndreyer 1973: 79) in the phonetic manifestation of the accent, and certain observations of Loewen (1958: 20, n. 4) even suggest the possibility that Sambú is a tone language … Nevertheless, for the moment, all authors agree in assigning the languages the status of accentual (stress) languages … In such words, in the cognate sets, the accent falls on the penultimate syllable almost without exception in Saija and Chamí.
tn.cite: Constenla Umaña, Adolfo & Margery Peña, Enrique. 1991. Elementos de fonología comparada chocó. Revista de Filología y Lingüística de la Universidad de Costa Rica 17(1-2): 137-191. doi:10.15517/rfl.v17i1-2.20972
tn.note: Not tonal: treated, with the other Emberá languages, as a stress-accent language whose accent is realised mainly by pitch; a possible tone contrast was raised only for Sambú (Northern Emberá).

632.dq: Stress often shifts to the penultimate syllable of a word when a suffix is added: warrá-rã 'son-PL', warra-rã́-pa 'son-PL-ERG'. (p.20; cf. p.7 'A word is composed of from one to seven syllables ... Nasality and stress function in relation to a syllable')
632.dloc: §1.5 pp.7-8 (general stress rule, ex. 18-20); §1.3 p.3; §2.1 pp.19-20 (nouns); §2.2-2.5 pp.20-21 (verbs); §2.6 p.24 (adjectives); p.26 (adverbs)
632.heavy: a word-final CVV syllable: a lengthened (geminate) vowel or a vowel sequence (VV/diphthong) in the ultimate syllable; all syllables are open, so closed syllables do not arise
632.prule: Stress normally on the penultimate syllable; if the ultimate syllable is CVV (geminate vowel or vowel sequence), stress falls on the first V of that final syllable (i.e. final stress). Grammatically imposed stress overrides the general rule: past/future tense and present-tense verbs stressed on the final (suffix) syllable even when CV (wã-hí), mood suffixes and imperatives give penult stress, habitual -pá is stressed; stress-only minimal pairs in inflection (če-hí PST vs čé-hi IMP; mí-a ERG vs mi-á DAT).
632.srule: Secondary stress on the first (word-initial) syllable, only in words of four or more syllables.
632.quote: [p.7] All syllables begin with a consonant (including the glottal stop) and are open. ... [p.8] Lengthened vowels are interpreted (and represented) as a sequence of two (geminate) vowels, but not two syllables, because they are stressed when they occur word final the same as any other VV series. ... Stress normally occurs on the penultimate syllable. However, if the ultimate syllable is CVV, stress occurs on the first V as shown in (19). (19) tapʰéda 'morning' čokʰára 'many' mikʰía 'rancid' waibía 'big'. Certain meaning differences are encoded only by contrastive stress. (20) če-hí 'come (PST…
632.loc: §1.5 pp.7-8 (general stress rule, ex. 18-20); §1.3 p.3; §2.1 pp.19-20 (nouns); §2.2-2.5 pp.20-21 (verbs); §2.6 p.24 (adjectives); p.26 (adverbs)
632.idn: Epena Pedee (Epérã Pedée; 'Saija'), Southern Emberá dialect cluster, Chocó family — the Saija/Guangüí river variety (not the divergent Basurudó dialect); data: Guangüí river area, tributary of the Saija river, Cauca, Pacific coast of Colombia; fieldwork 1977-1989…
632.exq_: [p.3] In the practical orthography and in texts, stress is written only where it is grammatically imposed, overriding the general stress rules. ... [p.20] Verbs in the past and future tenses are usually stressed on the final syllable which is typically a tense or number suffix ... (60) (a) wã-hí

morph.rootq: General rule is word-based: 'Stress normally occurs on the penultimate syllable. However, if the ultimate syllable is CVV, stress occurs on the first V' (§1.5, p.8). But the noun description refers to the root and to suffix syllable-count: 'Stress often shifts to the penultimate syllable of a word when a suffix is added: warrá-rã 'son-PL', warra-rã́-pa 'son-PL-ERG'. Nouns that have stress on the final syllable follow the same pattern, except there is no shift of stress in the noun if the suffix has only one syllable: kʰáu-rã 'daughter-PL'. When more than two syllables follow a noun, stress shifts from the noun root: kʰau-rã́-pa 'daughter-PL-ERG'.' (§2.1, pp.19-20); verbs: 'Verbs in the…
morph.elicq: 'This section is a summary and update of my phonological analysis written several years ago (Harms 1984, 1985).' (§1.4-1.7, p.4); 'Stress is marked above the nuclear vowel with an acute accent for the convenience of those who are unfamiliar with the stress patterns.' (§1.3, p.3); 'Data for this paper were gathered primarily in the Guanguí river area between the years 1977 and 1989.' (Acknowledgements, p.xiii). No statement of whether stress was determined from isolated words, frames, texts or measurements.
morph.stmt: 'All affixes in Epena Pedee are suffixes; there are no prefixes. Nouns can be marked by suffixes of case and number. Verbs may have suffixes of aspect, tense, number, and mood. This is characteristic of a typical SOV language.' (§1.10, p.13), with footnote 9: 'However, the generic morpheme ne- §3.9 could be viewed as a prefix.'
